title: An Intentional Way to Start 2026
author: Greg McKeown
summary: McKeown argues that the week between Christmas and New Year's is uniquely positioned for intentional planning. Rather than approaching 2026 with reactive task-lists, leaders should ask a central question: What actually matters now? This inquiry sits at the heart of Essentialism—the discipline of eliminating the nonessential. The Essentialism Planner is designed as a quarterly guide, breaking the year into 90-day cycles that feel actionable rather than abstract. McKeown advocates for a Personal Quarterly Offsite practice every three months to step back, eliminate noise, and decide what deserves best effort now, not someday. The planner uses simple tools like the Power Half Hour and the 1-2-3 Method to keep planning in service of priorities rather than competing with them. The core insight: intention in 90-day increments builds clarity and momentum better than a full-year vision.
points: The week between Christmas and New Year's offers rare quiet space to ask better questions—not what should I do next, but what actually matters now.
A 90-day planning horizon creates focus by being long enough to make real progress but short enough to stay intentional throughout.
The Personal Quarterly Offsite is a practice to return to every three months: step back, eliminate noise, and decide what deserves your best effort.
Planning tools must support priorities rather than compete with them; the 1-2-3 Method and Power Half Hour are designed to keep strategy visible without becoming burdensome.
Entering 2026 with intention means designing the next quarter around what truly matters, not what demands your attention.
quotes: This week, between Christmas and New Year's, has always felt different to me. The noise quiets down. The pace slows, just a little. And for just a moment, we get space to ask better questions.
Not: What should I do next? But: What actually matters now?

This planner isn't about organizing more tasks. It's about making deliberate choices—letting go of the nonessential so you can focus your limited time and energy on what truly matters, one quarter at a time.
This isn't just a planner. It's a quarterly guide to living a life you design.
I intentionally designed this as a 90-day planner. A full year can feel abstract. Ninety days creates focus. It's long enough to make real progress, and short enough to stay intentional.
One reader put it this way: This planner doesn't just plan your day. Its purpose is to help you achieve the important goals in your life.

If you want the next 90 days to be shaped by what truly matters—rather than by everything that demands your attention—the Essentialism Planner is designed to help you do exactly that.” Archived from Greg McKeown on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
